bull_bear.body: Capex prioritized for growth (INR100cr FY26); no dividend or buyback mentioned; no debt used; focus on internal funding and organic expansion
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 4-wheeler revenue conversion timeline risk; supply chain disruption for imported LED chips (mitigated by multi-sourcing); delay in ambient/adaptive lighting adoption by OEMs; macro slowdown in auto demand
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, bullish on 2-wheeler growth, strategically patient on 4-wheeler entry; emphasis on in-house R&D, localization, and innovation; avoids overpromising on guidance but signals clear momentum
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Fiem is the sole supplier of animation lighting on TVS Norton — a global first in 2-wheelers — creating a defensible tech moat; the INR2.5cr provision reversal is a one-time accounting benefit, not operational; 4-wheeler RFQs include Mercedes, indicating premium OEM validation
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Effectively debt-free: long term loans (Rs. in mn) were 508 in FY21 and 205 in FY22, then 0 in each of FY23, FY24, FY25 and FY26; the balance sheet shows nil non-current and nil current borrowings at 31.03.24, 31.03.25 and 31.03.26.
- Dividend per share (Rs., marked restated on post-bonus share capital basis) has been raised every year: FY21 8, FY22 10, FY23 15, FY24 20, FY25 30, FY26 40.
- Consolidated cash and cash equivalents were 2,060 mn at 31.03.24, 2,983 mn at 31.03.25 and 2,794 mn at 31.03.26; total equity rose from 8,869 mn to 12,150 mn over the same three balance-sheet dates.
- Returns improved through the period — the deck's chart shows ROCE 11.66% / 19.62% / 25.08% / 24.96% / 26.22% / 28.02% and ROE 8.55% / 15.60% / 19.85% / 20.16% / 21.25% / 22.62% for FY21 through FY26.
- Working capital days lengthened from 9 in FY21 to 22-23 mid-period and 47 in FY26, while book value per share (Rs.) rose 218 / 246 / 289 / 366 / 393 / 460 across FY21-FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: 2-wheeler: 97% of revenue; led penetration: 63.9% of lighting sales; key customers: TVS, Royal Enfield (6% rev), Yamaha, Hero, HMSI (25% rev); 4-wheeler: 3% of revenue; new awards: Mahindra HMSL, RR, fog, side repeater; RFQs active with Force Motors, Mercedes; no headlamp/taillamp awards yet but committed to entering all lamp types
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Deck describes FIEM as one of the leading manufacturers of Automotive Lighting & Signalling Equipment's and Rear View Mirrors in India, and among the first companies in India introducing LED lights in two wheelers; founded 1989 by Mr. J.K. Jain as Rahul Auto Private Limited and listed on BSE and NSE in 2006.
- Its major business comes from the two-wheeler segment — the FY26 automotive segment split is 2 Wheeler 97.15% / 4 Wheeler 2.85%.
- Strong client base of more than 50 OEMs, supplying prestigious customers since their inception: 2W — TVS, Honda, Yamaha, Suzuki, Royal Enfield, Harley Davidson, Hero Motocorp, Piaggio; 4W — Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, Force Motors, Ashok Leyland, Hyundai.
- Customer concentration is high and rising at the top: FY26 automotive segment contribution was TVS Motor Company 32.71%, Honda Two Wheeler Group 24.78%, India Yamaha 14.15%, Suzuki Motorcycle 9.25%, Royal Enfield 5.79%, Replacement Market 4.98%, Other Customers 8.34% (FY25: 27.84%, 27.80%, 14.90%, 9.25%, 4.60%, 5.67%, 9.94%).
- Exports go to Honda Japan, Harley Davidson (USA & Thailand) and Kubota Japan (tractors and farm equipment), besides OEMs in Austria, UK, Germany, Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam — though exports were only 1.85% of FY26 automotive segment revenue.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Leadership transition] With effect from June 01, 2026, founder Mr. J.K. Jain was re-designated Executive Chairman (from Chairman & Managing Director), Mr. Rahul Jain was elevated to Managing Director, and Ms. Aanchal Jain was re-designated Joint Managing Director; Mr. Rajesh Sharma continues as Joint Managing Director and Mr. Kashi Ram Yadav as Whole-time Director.
- [Bonus issue] FY22 and FY23 EPS figures in both the consolidated and standalone income statements, and several per-share charts, are footnoted RESTATED ON POST-BONUS SHARE CAPITAL BASIS.
- [Group structure] Wholly-owned subsidiaries are Fiem Industries Japan Co., Ltd. (Japan) and Fiem Research and Technology s.r.l (Italy); the JV company is Fiem Kyowa (HK) Mould Company Limited (Hong Kong), a 50:50 JV set up in 2017 with KYOWA Co., Ltd., Japan for high-class moulds and tools.
- [Fuel pump JV] In 2018 FIEM entered a Joint Venture with Aisan Industry Co. Ltd., Japan and Toyota Tsusho India Pvt. Ltd. for manufacture of Fuel Pump Module for the Indian market.
- [Regulatory approvals] The Integrated Passenger Information System with LED Display (IPIS) holds approval from the Ministry of Railways - Research Design and Standard Organization (RDSO) for train indication, coach guidance and PC-based announcement, and the Association of State Road Transport Undertakings inspected the LED based Destination system and found it satisfactory.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin improved to 13.93% (from 13.21% YoY) due to operating leverage (capacity utilization ~80%), higher LED mix, and in-house SMT/assembly localization (only LED chips imported); no raw material cost pressure cited
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 15-20% FY26; margin: targeting 13-14% range with upside to 14%; order inflow: expecting conversion of INR1,000-1,200cr RFQ pipeline over next 2 years; capex/commissioning: INR100cr total FY26 (INR50-60cr H2), no new plant commissioning date disclosed yet
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: >INR1,000 crores pipeline across 100+ projects; includes Mahindra (Bolero, Scorpio, XUV700), Hero (Glamour X125, Xtreme), Yamaha (XSR155, EV), TVS Norton (global), Force Motors, Mercedes RFQs
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 4-wheeler expansion (targeting >10% revenue share in 12–18 months); export growth via TVS Norton & Yamaha global models; ambient lighting commercialization (POC done); adaptive lighting via MOU with Allight Lighting; EV lighting for Yamaha and others
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Fiem delivered record Q2FY26 revenue and PAT driven by strong 2-wheeler demand and higher-margin LED product mix, while making strategic inroads into 4-wheeler lighting with new Mahindra awards and advanced tech like animation lighting — the shift from 3% to >10% 4-wheeler revenue share over the next 12–18 months is the key value driver.

open.item: Gogoro facing significant international headwinds; India strategy unclear and project on pause; investment under INR10 crores and reimbursable; tech transfer expected in next couple of quarters but may be delayed.
State-of-the-art EMC/EMI electronic validation lab (first of its kind in Indian auto lighting) under installation, to be commissioned in the next quarter.
Management expects H2 FY26 to be better and the full year could be the highest-ever two-wheeler production year, surpassing the FY19-20 peak.
Hero Glamour X 125 (projector headlamp) and Xtreme (LED winker) in production; more models under development, with next half expected even better for Hero.
Clearer four-wheeler business planning / revenue picture to be shared by end of this financial year, plus a direction on a dedicated plant.
Capex of INR38 cr in H1; expect another INR50-60 crores in H2, totaling ~INR100 crores for FY26, with momentum to continue in line with growth.
Company to add another 10 SMT lines over the next year, from the current 10 lines.
Company reiterates 15-20% revenue growth guidance for FY27 and belief it will outperform the industry; no specific numeric guidance beyond that.

At the Hosur facility, around 65% of energy needs are being met through open-access solar power, with a further ~20% being added through wind energy; renewable energy initiatives are being progressively rolled out to other plants.
open.promised: additional ~20% via wind (on top of ~65% solar) % of energy requirement

open.item: Reinstatement of Tapukara Unit-VIII (building, machinery, equipment damaged in the August 2025 fire) is under progress; interim production set-up for Bank Angle Sensor (BAS) and 4-Wheeler (especially M&M) parts was reinstated at the Rai Plant and restarted in September 2025, while undamaged Ground Floor/Basement production at Tapukara resumed 29 August 2025.
Company filed an estimated insurance claim of Rs.82.30 Crore with the Insurer/Surveyor for the August 2025 fire at Tapukara Unit-VIII and requested an ad-hoc payment; recovery outcome pending.

Board recommended (meeting held 30 May 2026) a final dividend of 400% (Rs.40 per equity share of Rs.10 each) for FY 2025-26, which if approved by members would involve a cash outflow of Rs.10,527.86 Lakh; subject to approval at the ensuing AGM.
open.promised: Rs.40/share (400%); cash outflow Rs.10527.86 Lakh if approved INR per share / INR lakh

open.item: Company commenced supplies to Mahindra & Mahindra during the year and, supported by a growing customer base and healthy order pipeline, remains confident of strengthening its position in the high-value four-wheeler lighting business.

Hosur facility to raise its renewable-energy share of power consumption by adding roughly 20% wind energy on top of the ~65% already met via open-access solar power; similar renewable-energy initiatives are being progressively rolled out across other manufacturing locations.
open.promised: additional ~20% via wind (on top of existing ~65% solar) % of energy requirement

open.item: Royal Enfield is ~6% of sales with >90% share on Classic lamps; management expects an uptick above 6% going forward on volumes and new models.
No stock split or bonus under discussion, having just completed a bonus in 2024.
Dutch chipmaker Nexperia global issues flagged; Fiem uses multi-source discrete electronic components so no production hold-up expected in coming months.
Ambient lighting proof-of-concept demonstrated and appreciated by a customer; company expects to be on the ambient light supplier panel very soon.
Four-wheeler RFQ value remains ~INR700 crores (some converted, new ones from Force Motors); RFQs also in progress with Mercedes; more than 100 projects overall worth ~INR1,000-1,200 crores.
Margin reached ~14% on product mix and operating leverage; management hoping to work around the 14% mark going forward (vs prior 13-14% guidance) and views it as sustainable.

verdicts.item: Products to be added to Hero Xtreme 125R very soon; 250R already started; Harley Davidson flagship projects ramping slowly plus upcoming exports.
verdicts.note: 'supplies has also started for Winker lamp for Hero Glamour and Xtreme models' — Xtreme in production; Glamour X 125 launched with projector headlamp.

verdicts.item: Working on ~10 Yamaha models (domestic and global); around 3 models expected to launch in coming quarters (Q2-Q4).
verdicts.note: Yamaha models launched (XSR 155, first EV, Tracer 7) with Fiem lighting; multiple export models to Brazil/Europe.

verdicts.item: No greenfield PV plant investment planned for the next two years; PV orders served from existing facilities until a big order justifies a new plant.
verdicts.note: PV still served from existing facilities (revenue 'insignificant'); a Pune warehouse being opened; dedicated-plant direction only 'by end of this financial year' — no greenfield yet.

verdicts.item: Hero models (waiting for launches) expected to work towards more than 10% of revenue over 3-4 years.
verdicts.note: 'once the customer gets to at least a 10% of our revenue, that's when we can... give a more specific guidance. Right now, it's much lower... This quarter has been much better' (Hero).

verdicts.item: Company to be ready with a proper four-wheeler business plan and share numbers by end of FY25.
verdicts.note: End-FY25 4W plan not delivered; now 'by end of this financial year, we should be having a clearer picture on our business planning.'

verdicts.item: Mahindra first number plate lamp approved for 3XO/Thar/Scorpio; second number plate approved for e-3-wheeler Supro and Bolero; production likely to commence Q1FY26.
verdicts.note: Mahindra number-plate lamp production established and 'adopted... in their Scorpio and Thar models' — Q1FY26 start achieved and scaling.

verdicts.item: Management reiterated generic 15-20% revenue growth guidance and said FY25 outlook is strong across all segments with rural demand back.
verdicts.note: 'we have given a guidance of 15% to 20% revenue growth, which we are maintaining' — reaffirmed.

verdicts.item: Management intends to work in a ~13-13.5% EBITDA margin band over the next couple of years; no quarter-by-quarter guidance.
verdicts.note: Q2 EBITDA margin 13.93% — above the ~13-13.5% band; 'we are hoping to work around the 14% mark going forward.'

verdicts.item: Management targets 15-20% revenue growth (definitely not less), continuing to outperform industry; expects FY26 demand momentum to continue.
verdicts.note: Q2 sales +17.12%, H1 +15.19%; '15% to 20% revenue growth, which we are maintaining' and 'we will outperform the industry.' [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Order book of more than 100 products to be developed over next 2 years, valued up to ~INR800 crores.
verdicts.note: 'we have more than 100 projects as of now that will be generating the revenue in years to come, maybe around INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores' — above the ~INR800 cr earlier stated.

verdicts.item: Two Hero models (incl. X440 Harley-Davidson) in production; two more to launch in next two quarters, with additional projects for FY25.
verdicts.note: 'There are two models which from Hero is being launched. It is being already converted into a mass production and a sales' (Glamour X 125, Xtreme winker).

verdicts.item: Capex guidance INR125-150 crores for FY25 (INR108 cr spent in 9M, ~INR25 cr in Q4) and INR75-100 crores additional next year, excluding any new greenfield four-wheeler plant.
verdicts.note: 'our capex for the current year should be INR100 crores' (H1 INR37.81 cr, +INR50-60 cr H2), in line with the earlier guidance; no greenfield 4W plant.

wtt.summary: 68% guidance hit (14 chains); 5/8 projects on-time; 15% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Highly confident on record numbers and margin sustainability at ~14%; owned Yamaha's softer quarter and PV revenue still being insignificant; deferred four-wheeler revenue and plant decisions to year-end as usual.

meta.thesis: Fiem delivered record Q2FY26 revenue and PAT driven by strong 2-wheeler demand and higher-margin LED product mix, while making strategic inroads into 4-wheeler lighting with new Mahindra awards and advanced tech like animation lighting — the shift from 3% to >10% 4-wheeler revenue share over the next 12–18 months is the key value driver.
